examples.question_text: A movie starts at $5{:}45$ pm and lasts $1$ hour $35$ minutes. When does it finish? Give your answer in 12-hour time.
examples.solution_text:
$5{:}45\text{ pm}=17{:}45$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}17{:}45+1\text{ h }35\text{ min}\\&=19{:}20\end{aligned}$
The movie finishes at $7{:}20$ pm.

examples.question_text: A train journey lasts $2$ hours $25$ minutes and finishes at $01{:}10$ on Wednesday. When did it start? Give the day and 24-hour time.
examples.solution_text:
Subtract the hours, crossing back into Tuesday, then subtract the minutes.
$\begin{aligned}01{:}10-2\text{ h}&=23{:}10\text{ on Tuesday}\\23{:}10-25\text{ min}&=22{:}45\end{aligned}$
The journey started at $22{:}45$ on Tuesday.

examples.question_text: A workshop starts at $9{:}45$ am and ends at $2{:}20$ pm on the same day. How long does it last?
examples.solution_text:
$2{:}20\text{ pm}=14{:}20$
Borrow $1$ hour as $60$ minutes before subtracting.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}14\text{ h }20\text{ min}-9\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=13\text{ h }80\text{ min}-9\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=4\text{ h }35\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A coach leaves at $22{:}35$ on Friday. The journey takes $4$ hours $50$ minutes. What day and time does it arrive?
examples.solution_text:
Carry $60$ minutes as $1$ hour.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}22{:}35+4\text{ h }50\text{ min}\\&=27{:}25\end{aligned}$
Subtract $24$ hours to find the time on the next day.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}27{:}25-24\text{ h}\\&=03{:}25\end{aligned}$
The coach arrives at $03{:}25$ on Saturday.

examples.question_text:
A movie lasts $154$ minutes.
(a) When does it finish if it starts at $14{:}50$?
(b) When does it start if it finishes at $12{:}15$?
examples.solution_text:
$154\text{ min}=120\text{ min}+34\text{ min}=2\text{ h }34\text{ min}$
(a)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}14{:}50+2\text{ h }34\text{ min}\\&=17{:}24\end{aligned}$
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}12{:}15-2\text{ h }34\text{ min}\\&=09{:}41\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A camper leaves at $7{:}40$ am on Saturday and returns at $6{:}25$ pm on Monday. How long is the camper away? Give your answer in days, hours and minutes.
examples.solution_text:
$7{:}40\text{ am}=07{:}40$ and $6{:}25\text{ pm}=18{:}25$.
Monday is two days after Saturday, so add $48$ hours to the end time.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}18{:}25+48\text{ h}\\&=66{:}25\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}66\text{ h }25\text{ min}-7\text{ h }40\text{ min}\\&=65\text{ h }85\text{ min}-7\text{ h }40\text{ min}\\&=58\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=2\text{ days }10\text{ h }45\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A journey starts at $10{:}35$ pm and ends at $4{:}15$ am the next day. How long does it last?
examples.solution_text:
$10{:}35\text{ pm}=22{:}35$ and $4{:}15\text{ am}=04{:}15$.
Add $24$ hours to the end time because it is on the next day.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}04{:}15+24\text{ h}\\&=28{:}15\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}28\text{ h }15\text{ min}-22\text{ h }35\text{ min}\\&=27\text{ h }75\text{ min}-22\text{ h }35\text{ min}\\&=5\text{ h }40\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A bus must arrive at $06{:}20$. Driving takes $2$ hours $35$ minutes, and boarding takes $20$ minutes before departure. What is the latest time boarding can begin?
examples.solution_text:
Subtract the driving time, then the boarding time.
$\begin{aligned}06{:}20-2\text{ h }35\text{ min}&=03{:}45\\03{:}45-20\text{ min}&=03{:}25\end{aligned}$
Boarding can begin at $03{:}25$.

coverage.summary: Authored eight editable worked examples covering all distinct accepted assessment methods with different values. Manual carrying and borrowing follow the accepted theory and retain the booklet's add/subtract approach at Stage 3 level. Questions and solutions are separate; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Continuation expressions have phantom equals gutters; independent equations retain their own left-hand sides. No diagrams are needed for these calculation methods. Assessments were classified only, without alteration or renewed audit. No files were written; independent review and actual visual capture remain coordinator stages.

examples.derivation: 17:45 plus 1 hour is 18:45; adding 35 minutes gives 19:20, or 7:20 pm.
01:10 Wednesday minus 2 hours is 23:10 Tuesday; subtracting 25 minutes gives 22:45 Tuesday.
2:20 pm is 14:20. Renaming 14 hours 20 minutes as 13 hours 80 minutes and subtracting 9 hours 45 minutes gives 4 hours 35 minutes.
35 plus 50 minutes is 85 minutes, or 1 hour 25 minutes. The extended finish is 27:25; subtracting 24 hours gives 03:25 Saturday.
154 minutes is 2 hours 34 minutes. (a) 14:50 plus this duration gives 17:24. (b) 12:15 minus 2 hours gives 10:15; subtracting 34 minutes gives 09:41.
Saturday to Monday contributes 48 hours. Adding 48 hours to 18:25 gives 66:25; subtracting 07:40 gives 58 hours 45 minutes, equal to 2 days 10 hours 45 minutes.
The start is 22:35 and the next-day finish is 04:15. Adding 24 hours makes the finish 28:15; subtracting 22:35 gives 5 hours 40 minutes.
06:20 minus 2 hours 35 minutes gives departure at 03:45. Subtracting the preceding 20-minute boarding period gives 03:25.

review.summary: All eight examples pass independent mathematical and supplied-source review. The 21 exact assessment locators are mapped, and all nine mapped methods have example coverage. Manual carrying and borrowing fit the accepted theory and Stage 3 scope; no syllabus exception is needed. Separate question and solution fields, phantom gutters and plain solution prose meet the supplied requirements. Diagrams are unnecessary. There are no existing examples to audit. Accepted assessments were classified only; their mathematics was not re-audited. Actual rendering and label-size verification remain for the coordinator’s visual stage.
